title: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies - National Values Education - Dangers of Drug Trafficking
exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
subject: National Values Education

questions.q: According to the Social Studies syllabus, what is the exact meaning of **Drug Trafficking**?
options: The legal dispensing of drugs by licensed medical pharmacists
The illegal manufacturing, distribution, and transportation of prohibited narcotic drugs and psychoactive substances
The process of swallowing prescribed medicine for personal healing
The act of exporting legally produced agricultural medicine
questions.explain: **Drug Trafficking** is an illicit global trade involving the illegal cultivation, manufacture, distribution, and sale of substances which are subject to drug prohibition laws.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which of the following describes how **Greed** acts as a major reason for trafficking in drugs?
options: The intense, selfish desire to acquire wealth rapidly without doing any legitimate hard work
The lack of formal education regarding international laws
The state of having no money to feed one's family
The desire to cure sick people in foreign countries
questions.explain: **Greed** refers to an insatiable desire for wealth. Many traffickers are already financially stable but engage in the illicit trade strictly because of the 'get-rich-quick' syndrome.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Sometimes, innocent youths are deceived into carrying luggage containing hidden drugs across international borders because they lack knowledge of the contents. This reason is categorized under:
questions.explain: **Ignorance** is a major factor. Unsuspecting individuals (often called 'blind mules') can be tricked into carrying drugs due to a lack of awareness or education about the tactics of drug cartels.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q:
Consider the equation representing the root causes of the drug trade:
$$ \text{Vulnerability} = \text{Ignorance} + X $$
If $X$ represents the socio-economic condition of being unable to afford basic human needs, driving people to desperate measures, what is $X$?
questions.explain: **Poverty** represents extreme financial hardship. Drug cartels frequently exploit impoverished citizens by offering them large sums of money to risk their lives trafficking drugs.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: What is an immediate danger faced by citizens of a country heavily associated with drug trafficking when they travel internationally?
options: They receive automatic visas and warm welcomes
They are given bad image, often resulting in severe stigmatization, harassment, and intense security scrutiny at foreign airports
They are mandated to pay lower international taxes
They are immediately drafted into foreign militaries
questions.explain: A prominent danger of drug trafficking is that it creates a **bad image for the country**. Innocent citizens suffer extreme stigmatization and dehumanizing searches abroad.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: In several Asian and Middle Eastern countries, what is the ultimate legal penalty specifically prescribed for drug trafficking?
options: A warning letter from the embassy
questions.explain: To serve as a maximum deterrent, many countries strictly enforce the **death penalty** for anyone caught smuggling illicit drugs across their borders.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: How does the illegal drug trade directly **affect national security**?
options: It decreases the nation's unemployment rate permanently
Drug cartels use massive illegal profits to buy advanced weapons, fund terrorism, and corrupt law enforcement agencies
It forces citizens to become more patriotic
It provides governments with more taxes for the military
questions.explain: The massive, untraceable wealth generated by trafficking is frequently used to finance heavily armed cartels, insurgencies, and systemic corruption, gravely threatening **national security**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: One of the effective ways of discouraging youths from drug abuse and trafficking is forming peer-driven associations in schools known as:
questions.explain: Just like the Road Safety Club, establishing **Drug Free Clubs** in schools creates a positive peer environment that actively advocates against substance abuse.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which coping skill involves the ability to confidently express your beliefs and stand your ground against peer pressure without becoming aggressive?
questions.explain: **Assertiveness** is a critical psychological coping skill. It allows a youth to confidently say "No" to drugs and firmly stand by their personal values under peer pressure.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q:
Analyze the table mapping coping skills to their functions:

| Coping Skill | Function against Drug Abuse |
|---|---|
| Refusal/Resistance skills | The ability to politely but firmly reject an offer to consume drugs |
| $Y$ | The ability to analyze a difficult life situation and find a healthy solution without using drugs as an escape |

Which of the following correctly replaces $Y$?
questions.explain: **Problem solving skills** involve confronting life's challenges directly and formulating rational solutions rather than turning to psychoactive substances as a means of escape.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: When a student proactively engages in sporting activities, attends vocational training, or participates in religious events after school hours to avoid bad company, this is termed:
questions.explain: Idleness is a major trigger for delinquency. Engaging in sports or productive hobbies represents a **constructive use of time**, keeping youths safely occupied and away from drug peddlers.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: If a teenager realizes their current peer group often skips classes to smoke marijuana and subsequently decides to distance themselves to join a study group, which preventative strategy is applied?
questions.explain: Because peer influence is heavily tied to socialization, consciously **choosing good friends** who possess positive moral values is a direct way to discourage drug abuse.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: In the process of discouraging drug abuse, developing **Communication Skills** is vital because it allows youths to:
options: Effectively articulate their feelings and distress to parents or counselors instead of using drugs to cope
Secretly message drug cartels online without being caught
Learn multiple foreign languages for international trafficking
Incite violent mass actions on social media platforms
questions.explain: **Communication skills** help youths build strong support networks. They can express their emotional pains or stressors to trusted adults, rather than resorting to substance abuse as an outlet.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: When comparing positive group behaviour to the actions of a drug cartel, a cartel is a prime example of a group exhibiting:
questions.explain: Because a cartel's activities directly inflict addiction, violence, and death upon society, it represents the epitome of **destructive (negative) group behaviour**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: If a brilliant university graduate cannot find employment and subsequently decides to ferry hard drugs across the border to survive, what fundamental reason for trafficking is demonstrated?
questions.explain: The scenario perfectly depicts how systemic **Poverty and Unemployment** breed desperation, pushing even educated individuals into illicit trades to secure a livelihood.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education
